subject: general
question: If x = –2, y = 3, Quantity A = -x²y³ and Quantity B = 0, then which of the following statements is correct with respect to Quantities A and B?

options.text: Both Quantities A and B are equal.

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the signs: **Quantity A** = −(negative)eveⁿ × (positive)odd.

−x²y³ = −(−2)²(3)³ ⇒ −(4)(27) ⇒ **Negative Value**.

Since **Quantity A** is negative and **Quantity B** is zero, 0 > negative.

**∴ The correct answer is Quantity B is greater.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x = −2, y = 3, **Quantity A** = −x²y³, **Quantity B** = 0.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3daf6885876973d2b2d30486ce808661c4e52167f082665de66908b853f31ef2.png] 

⇒ Substitute the values in **Quantity A**:

⇒ Quantity A = −(−2)² × (3)³

⇒ Quantity A = −(4) × (27)

⇒ Quantity A = −108

⇒ Compare with **Quantity B**: −108 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Power of Negative Numbers

(−a)ⁿ is positive if n is an **even integer** and negative if n is an **odd integer**.

Comparison with Zero

Any **positive number** is always greater than 0, and any **negative number** is always less than 0.

BODMAS in Algebra

Always solve **exponents** before applying the leading negative sign in expressions like −xⁿ.</p
